quote.translation: That in this passage jinen ni and onozukara have exactly the same meaning rests on the same Ground as Plato's treating nature and chance as of one kind (see p. 78).

quote.translation: In short, the indeterminate spontaneity of onozukara, as causal contingency, turns through heterogeneous combination in the direction of teleological necessity and becomes the freedom of mizukara, and conversely runs through homogeneous combination in the direction of teleological contingency and becomes jinen, that is, nature.

regions.text: 、それと反對に同種結合によつて目々偶然の方向へ走つて「じねん」すなはち自郷となるのである。

quote.translation: Freedom and nature thus stand in direct opposition to one another.

quote.translation: If ten or twenty thousand seeds are sown each year and this is continued for ten years, the seeds sown first will bear fruit from the fourth or fifth year onwards, so that within ten years they can be cultivated step by step.

quote.translation: Hegel's distinction between freedom (Freiheit) and arbitrariness (Willkür) likewise sets up, on the one side, mizukara, in which teleological necessity is most strongly emphasised, as "freedom", and on the other calls "arbitrariness" the result of the homogeneous combination of the causal contingency of onozukara with the teleological contingency of jinen.
